newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices end up, volume declines.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices end up, volume declines.

text.p: China's stock markets on Monday put aside fears over the suspension last Friday of several companies in the A share market and ended up, although on sharply reduced trading volume, analysts said.

The Shanghai B index inched up 0.521 points or 0.62 percent to 84.959 points on thin volume of 11.024 million shares worth $7.711 million, while the Shenzhen B index surged 7.79 points or 4.89 percent to 166.85 points on turnover of HK$105.9 million.
"Some risk-takers jumped in to buy after seeing that Shenzhen Development Bank did not pull down the markets when it resumed trading in the afternoon," a broker at China Guotai Securities said.

Large-capitalisation Shenzhen Development Bank Co's A shares -- which were suspended in the morning after the bank announced it might have been involved in stock trading irregularities -- closed at 36.97 yuan, down just 0.17 yuan.
A handful of other firms also had their shares suspended to allow for investigation into sharp fluctuations in share prices in recent days.
"The price (of Shenzhen Development Bank's shares) did not plunge because the dividend plan remained intact," the Guotai broker said.

The bank said that although it was investigating possible stock trading irregularities in 1996, plans to make a five-for-10 bonus share issue and 0.2 yuan per share cash dividend based on 1996 profits were unchanged.

"But the small trading volume shows people are nervous after the indices slid last week, following the suspension of several stocks," an analyst at J&A Securities said. "We are going to see volatile trading ahead."
In the B share market, Shenzhen Merchants Shekou Port Service Holdings Co Ltd was the top gainer, rising HK$0.47 or 9.94 percent to HK$5.20.

On the Shanghai B share market, institutional support buying in market barometer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development pulled the index up, but heavy profit-taking limited its rise, brokers said.
"Market sentiment has been hurt by the government's recent clampdown, but some institutions which hold large positions in Lujiazui still tried to push its price up," said one broker.
"With trading volume so thin, upward potential will be limited," another broker said. "Investor concerns about possible further crackdown measures may pull the index down again."
Shanghai Kaikai Industrial Co was the star on a technical rebound, jumping $0.036 or 8.69 percent to $0.450 on volume of 327,000 shares.
Lujiazui was the most actively traded on institutional support, up $0.054 or 3.86 percent to $1.450 on volume of 1.9 million shares.
The Shanghai A index gained 30.562 points or 2.22 percent to 1,406.472 points on volume of 529.1 million shares worth 6.8 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index jumped 135.703 points or 3.58 percent to 3,922.289 points.
The Shenzhen A index rose 5.07 points or 1.08 percent to 472.43 on turnover of 6.7 billion yuan.
